title: Resilient VPC Egress Controller: Terraform module for subnet routing, NAT failover, and endpoint health automation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a reusable Terraform module (resilient-vpc-egress-controller) that codifies subnet allocation, route table orchestration, NAT gateway / IGW provisioning, AZ-aware NAT failover, and automated VPC endpoint health probes. This module is intended for Redwood Private deployments (VPC + on-prem variants) and must include upgrade-safe defaults, clear inputs for customer network topologies, and an automated health-checking mechanism (Lambda or provider-native) that reconciles unhealthy endpoints and flips routes to warm standby NATs. The module must be compatible with existing networking IaC patterns used across Private and Dedicated offerings and include a migration plan for clusters using manual NAT/route setups.
acceptance_criteria: Module accepts explicit subnet map (public/private/isolated) and can derive route tables per AZ
AZ-aware NAT failover: when a NAT in an AZ reports unhealthy, routes update to a warm NAT in the same AZ or fallback to cross-AZ pool based on policy
VPC endpoints (S3, DynamoDB, custom interface endpoints) are created with correct policies and route propagation where relevant
Health checks run every 30s (configurable) and surface to a monitoring dashboard/alerting rule
Module has terraform tests (unit / integration via terratest) and a documented upgrade path that preserves IP allocations and existing route tables
Automation does not assume any specific cloud account structure and supports passing existing resources (e.g., preexisting IGW) instead of recreating them
tasks: Design module interface: variables, outputs, and policy knobs (team + review)
Implement subnet and route table resources with per-AZ mapping
Implement NAT pool provisioning with tags for warm-standby and active roles
Add health-checking component (Lambda + CloudWatch or provider-managed probe) and IAM roles
Create VPC endpoint module wiring for gateway and interface endpoints with optional private DNS
Write terratest integration that deploys a small cluster and simulates NAT failure to validate failover
Document upgrade/migration steps and compatibility notes in README
Create example var files for common topologies (3-AZ, single-AZ fallback, on-prem peering)
Security review and threat model review with SecOps
Prepare RFC and announce migration schedule to infra teams
comments: 2026-03-02 - Asha: Kickoff retro. Agreed module should avoid implicit resource deletion and require 'manage_existing' flags for IGW/NAT if user wants to keep them.

2026-03-04 - Daniel: Initial interface PR posted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-terraform/pull/1286 — includes var schema and stubbed outputs. Requesting design review from @marta and @li.

2026-03-05 - Marta (Networking): We should expose a 'failover_policy' enum (prefer-local, cross-az, global) and an 'ttl' for route changes so BGP peers can converge. Also called out need for explicit IAM least-privilege for health probe.

2026-03-06 - Daniel: Implemented health probe as modular opt-in: provider_native_probe = true enables cloud-provider healthcheck resource, otherwise fallback to small lambda. PR updated: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-terraform/pull/1299
2026-03-08 - Security: SecOps requested a design note on endpoint policies; added requirement for deny-listing by default and an 'allowed_services' whitelist in README.

2026-03-09 - QA: Started terratest harness against a staging account; initial run passed for resource creation. Observed 12s median route propagation time in us-west-2 which is within tolerance; recording results in test dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/net-provisioning/tests/ENG-74322

2026-03-10 - Daniel: Marking first implementation ready for internal review. Need sign-off on upgrade strategy and runbook from platform-ops before merging. Next: resilience chaos test to intentionally drop NAT ENIs and verify routing flips.
TO-DO: coordinate with infra-privops for statefile locking and terraform version constraints
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): deploy module to a single sandbox VPC in staging with provider_native_probe=true and monitor for 72h
Phase 1 (internal): enable module for Platform team workloads in a dedicated account, run chaos tests (drop NAT, deny route propagation) and validate rollback
Phase 2 (customer pilot): offer module to 1–2 early Private customers as opt-in for next provisioning cycle
Phase 3 (GA): flip default to module-managed NATs for new VPCs and publish migration guide for existing customers
testing_plan: Unit tests for input validation and plan-only diffs
Terratest integration: create whole VPC, deploy NATs, simulate NAT failure (detach ENI) and assert route table updates within configured TTL
Load test: validate route churn under 100 RPS of provisioning API calls
Chaos monkey: scheduled NAT termination to verify automated failovers and monitoring alerts trigger
Security test: run terraform-compliance and KICS scans against module templates
monitoring_playbook: Create dashboard: VPC-Provisioning / ENG-74322 showing: NAT health states, route-change latency, endpoint error rates, terraform apply success/failure
Alert: NAT-Health-Critical -> PagerDuty when >1 AZ reports NAT unhealthy for 2 consecutive probes
Alert: Route-Propagation-Delay -> Slack when median propagation > 60s in any AZ
upgrade_path: Non-destructive by default: module exposes 'manage_existing' flags for IGW, route-tables, and NATs so existing resources are adopted rather than recreated
Provide a migration script for map-based subnets -> new subnet module variables (preserves subnet IDs and route associations)
Backwards compatibility shim: when older layouts detected, module sets 'compat_mode' to avoid changing route names/tags
Automated preflight (terraform plan) output checks to alert on any replacement operations before apply
risk_mitigation: Require manual approval for any apply that contains resource replacements in production
Limit rollout concurrency to 1 VPC per account per day during canary
Add feature flags in private provisioning pipeline to quickly revert to manual NAT routing
Keep warm standbys sized to handle expected cross-AZ egress until autoscaling is validated
